differences.what: Residual table: A lists the orthogonal residual subspace of every edge type (B(x)t_X^perp, P(x)t_X^perp, B(x)F, P(x)F, B(x)<t_Y>, (B(x)t_Y^perp)perp(P(x)<t_X>), P(x)<t_Y>, (A(x)F)(x)Q^perp) as well as its dimension; B lists the dimensions of all edges but names only the 2->5 residual.

Orthonormal basis over F_2: B states that nonzero residuals are nonalternating and that alternating planes are absorbed through w+a, w+b, w+a+b. A asserts the orthonormal basis with 'hence' and no absorption step, and glosses the norm-one vector as a single coordinate unit.

Neither plan gives the liminf argument. A says the bound refutes the n log n optimality conjecture (S0). B says no fixed machine in the model needs Omega(n log n) (S0). Each states only the conclusion (379-387).

chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route in the same order: bank exchange, frames, nested labels with L<N/2, the two interfaces with s<Wm, eta>20*2^{-50} giving tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, then the interchange and layer recurrences with factor s/W on V/W streams, the synthetic transforms and convolution, resampling with chirp and permutation cancellation, assembly, exact recovery and the cost table. Neither breaks or thins out. B gathers the exponent into one recursive-power-saving step (S3.5), although its s_c is derived only later (S3.7.1.4). A puts tau and sigma after both interfaces (S2.5.0, S2.6.3.13). B also states the stream primitives behind the O(V) node costs, which A only cites; this is off the central chain.

errors.says: Every nonzero edge residual contains a norm-one vector, namely 'a coordinate unit outside the supports involved', hence has an orthonormal basis.
errors.paper: The norm-one vector is built by tensoring chosen norm-one vectors in each tensor summand: the triple-tensor vectors spanning P and Q, and coordinate units in B, in triple complements and in full spaces. Residuals with a P or Q factor contain no coordinate unit of F^{(x)3}. The orthonormal basis then needs the absorption of alternating planes.

overall.reason: Both plans carry the central chain and every checklist sub-step of the six discriminating results, with no major error. A writes out more of some constructions: the Gaussian maps and normalizations, the residual subspaces, and the general definitions of nu and C_1. B states the stream-operation lemmas that A omits entirely, the alternating-plane absorption and the layer's hypotheses. A also has one minor gloss error on the norm-one vectors. These differences are slight or concern a supporting result, they point both ways, and I cannot say which set weighs more.
